_note: T-4191: which mechanism should have caught each steer root (plugin/data/steer-roots.json), and the ledger event kinds it writes when it acts. When one root or one concern recurs 3 times in 7 days the recurrence pass (steerrecur.py) files 'why did <short> not catch it' and lists the mechanism's last firings from these kinds; the fix is to that mechanism, never a new one beside it. A root is a row here, no code. short: the name in the task's title; mechanism: what it is; match: an optional {data key: value} a firing's data must hold (several mechanisms share one kind).

R1.mechanism: the prompt hold that carries the standing instructions and the user's earlier corrections into a turn (UserPromptSubmit hook, steer expansion)

R2.mechanism: the sibling sweep that looks for the same fault elsewhere after a fix (miss ledger, fm miss)

R3.mechanism: the idle-stop hook that keeps a session going while the queue holds work it may do

R4.mechanism: the guard that blocks an action taken on state it never read (PreToolUse guard)

R5.mechanism: the correction hook that records a rejected approach and shows it again

R6.mechanism: the stop gate that holds a turn while a complaint or question of the user is waiting

R7.mechanism: the unproven-claim check that reads a 'done' against the task's evidence

R8.mechanism: the ship gate that checks the work is reachable by the user (merge, push, release)

concern.mechanism: the concerns repeat pass (sampo concerns act, run by sampo steers --tick), which files or reopens a task when a concern is said again
